title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Morgan Lee
summary: Comprehensive People Ops playbook covering hiring processes, structured onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, manager responsibilities, and common templates and checklists used across Redwood Inference.
content:
Purpose

This document is the canonical People Ops playbook for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance cycles, and manager responsibilities at Redwood Inference. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers as a day-one reference.

Quick links
- Hiring checklist (section 2)
- Interview scorecard & rubric (section 3)
- Offer & approval flow (section 4)
- New hire onboarding checklist (section 5)
- Performance & feedback cycles (section 6)
- Manager guide: 1:1s, calibration, and development (section 7)

1) Scope and principles
- Scope: Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires globally unless local law or a signed agreement supersedes this playbook.
- Principles: fairness, transparency, candidate experience, speed, documentation, and alignment to company values.
- Ownership: People Ops maintains the process; hiring managers are responsible for role definition, interview execution, and offer decisions.

2) Hiring process (high-level)
Overview: The standard hiring funnel at Redwood is: Requisition -> Sourcing -> Screen -> Onsite/Loop -> Decision -> Offer -> Hire. Target time-to-offer: 21 calendar days for most IC roles; 28 days for senior/manager hires.

Step-by-step procedure:
1. Requisition creation (Hiring manager + People Ops)
   - Required: role summary, impact statement, success criteria (3 bullets), proposed level/compensation band, proposed interview panel.
   - People Ops action: create req in ATS, confirm hiring authority and budget.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Passive sourcing by Recruiting; hiring manager provides prioritized skills and ideal experience.
   - Phone screen (30 min) to validate fundamentals and alignment. Use the Screening Checklist template.
3. Interview loop (typically 3-5 interviews)
   - Standard loop components: technical/core skills, system design (if applicable), product sense, behavioral/culture fit, and role-specific exercise.
   - Interviewers must use the standardized scorecard and submit feedback within 48 hours.
4. Debrief & decision
   - Hiring manager convenes panel within 72 hours of loop completion to discuss feedback and reach decision. Use unanimous or 2/3 approval depending on level.
5. Offer approval & extension (section 4)
6. Reference checks & background (as required by role)
7. Offer acceptance and start-date confirmation
8. Onboarding planning (People Ops + Manager)

Interview panel composition rules:
- Minimum 3 interviewers for mid-senior IC roles.
- Include at least one peer-level engineer and one cross-functional partner where relevant (PM, SRE, Data).
- For manager hires include upward manager or director in panel.
- Diverse panels encouraged; People Ops will advise where panels lack representation.

3) Interview scorecard & rubric
- Scorecard fields (required): role, candidate name, interviewer name, date, competency area, score 1-5, mandatory red flags, written notes, recommended action (strong hire/hold/reject).
- Rubric summary:
  - 5 = Exceptional: far exceeds expectations for level.
  - 4 = Strong: meets and occasionally exceeds expectations.
  - 3 = Satisfactory: meets expectations.
  - 2 = Below expectations: gaps that are addressable but notable.
  - 1 = Unsatisfactory: does not meet minimum expectations.
- Red-flag policy: Any interviewer marking a hard fail (1) must surface the concern during debrief and provide evidence in the scorecard. Single hard fail can veto hire for junior roles; for senior roles panel should discuss and document a path forward.

4) Offer & approval flow
Checklist before extending an offer:
- Finalized compensation band and equity grant (People Ops + Hiring manager)
- Approval from Finance for budget confirmation (if > band or special exception)
- Approval from Hiring Manager and Head of Org (for manager+ roles)
- Completed reference checks (role-dependent)
- Background check initiation instructions provided to candidate (if required)

Offer extension steps:
1. Hiring manager and People Ops agree on final package.
2. People Ops generates offer letter using the standard template and emails candidate.
3. Candidate negotiates (People Ops leads salary/equity discussions).
4. Once accepted, People Ops triggers preboarding tasks and sends new-hire welcome packet.

5) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)
Goals: accelerate new employee to full productivity, ensure clarity of expectations, and connect them to team and company culture.

Onboarding phases and checklists:
- Preboarding (1-14 days before start):
  - Send welcome packet, org chart, first-week schedule, Slack invite, and required forms (tax/benefit where applicable).
  - Manager assigns buddy and onboarding project.
- Day 1-7 (orientation & access):
  - Company orientation session (People Ops) covering values, handbook, security policies, benefits overview.
  - Provision accounts: SSO, Git repos, Jira, Confluence, internal dashboards, email.
  - Manager: 1:1 scheduled daily or every-other-day, review 30/60/90 goals.
- Week 2-4 (ramp and early impact):
  - First deliverable assigned (small project) with clear acceptance criteria.
  - Regular check-ins: weekly 1:1, weekly engineering team standups, and cross-functional intros.
- Month 1-3 (goal alignment & feedback):
  - 30/60/90 progress review with manager and People Ops touchpoint at day 45.
  - Formal 90-day checkpoint documenting outcomes, areas of support, and next steps.

Onboarding checklist table (text format)
| Item | Owner | Timeline | Status notes |
| Provision SSO & accounts | IT / People Ops | Day 0 |
| Assign buddy | Manager | Day 0 |
| Safety & security training | Security | Week 1 |
| First deliverable assigned | Manager | Week 2 |
| 30/60/90 goals set | Manager + Employee | Day 7 |

Manager onboarding responsibilities (first 30 days)
- Prepare role-specific onboarding plan and first deliverable.
- Schedule recurring 1:1 cadence (recommended weekly).
- Invite to team rituals and early cross-functional meetings.
- Host warm introductions to key stakeholders.

6) Performance and feedback cycles
Cadence and timeline:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged at least monthly via 1:1s and ad-hoc notes on Confluence/Hudson (internal feedback tool).
- Formal cycles: biannual performance reviews (mid-year and year-end) for all full-time employees.
- Calibration: Managers submit recommendations; Org leaders convene calibration panels to align leveling and ratings.

Review components:
- Self-assessment (employee)
- Manager assessment with examples linked to goals and impact
- Peer feedback (selected peers invited)
- Calibration review (org-level)

Rating scale and expectations (text summary):
- Exceeds Expectations: consistently delivers above scope, measurable impact.
- Meets Expectations: reliable delivery at level with some stretch outcomes.
- Needs Improvement: gaps in delivery/behavior; documented plan required.

Performance improvement process:
- If an employee is rated Needs Improvement or shows persistent gaps, the manager and People Ops will create a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with clear success metrics, timeline (typically 60-90 days), and checkpoints.
- PIP outcome options: successful improvement (transition back to growth plan), extended support, role change, or separation.

Compensation & promotion guidance:
- Promotion criteria: demonstration of consistent impact at the target level, ownership of cross-team initiatives, and proficiency in leadership behaviors for manager levels.
- Compensation adjustments are informed by market data, internal equity, role impact, and budget. People Ops owns pay market analysis and provides recommended ranges.

7) Manager guide: ongoing responsibilities and best practices
1:1s and feedback
- Recommended structure for weekly 1:1s (30-45 minutes):
  - Quick personal check-in (5 min)
  - Progress on goals & blockers (10-15 min)
  - Career development / feedback (10 min)
  - Action items recap (5 min)
- Document 1:1 notes in the team 1:1 template in Confluence to preserve context.

Career development & growth conversations
- Have quarterly development conversations to update career plan, skill targets, and stretch assignments.
- Use the promotion rubric and examples when preparing promotion packets.

Coaching and difficult conversations
- Use the STAR method for behavior feedback: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- Deliver balanced feedback: specific examples, expected behavior, and clear next steps.
- Escalate to People Ops if behavior concerns or potential legal/HR risks arise.

Calibration and cross-team alignment
- Attend calibration sessions prepared with evidence and cross-functional context.
- Avoid anchoring by not sharing prior performance ratings; focus on demonstrated impact and evidence.

Templates & examples (appendix)
- Screening checklist (text snippet):
  - Must-have skills:
    - X years relevant experience
    - Specific technical skill or domain knowledge
  - Nice-to-have skills:
    - Familiarity with infra or ML inference systems
  - Cultural fit questions:
    - Tell me about a time you shipped a complex system under tight constraints.
- 30/60/90 goals template (text snippet):
  - 30 days: Learn systems, meet stakeholders, complete first small task.
  - 60 days: Deliver meaningful component, reduce area of technical debt.
  - 90 days: Fully owner of a product slice and measurable impact.
- Offer letter checklist: candidate name, start date, compensation, equity, manager name, reporting location, conditions (background).

Common scenarios & guidance
- Internal transfers: require manager-to-manager conversation and People Ops approval. Use the internal mobility form.
- Remote hires & equipment: People Ops coordinates device ship and stipend within 5 business days of acceptance.
- International hires & visa support: People Ops will partner with legal; timeline varies by country.

Escalation & dispute resolution
- If hiring disputes occur (e.g., conflicting panel feedback), hiring manager escalates to People Ops with panel feedback and hiring rationale. People Ops will mediate and recommend next steps within 3 business days.
- For performance disputes, follow documented appeals process: request review by People Ops and Head of Org.

Appendix: useful links and resources
- People Ops portal (on Confluence): /confluence/people-ops
- Recruiting templates & scorecards: /confluence/people-ops/recruiting-templates
- Onboarding new hire packet: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-packet
- Promotion & compensation guidelines: /confluence/people-ops/compensation

Document maintenance
- Owners: People Ops.
- Review cadence: annual or as needed when policies change.
- Contact: people-ops@redwood-inference.internal for questions or exceptions.
